questions.q: What does the bus metaphor show about organizations?
a: Everyone must contribute for the group to move
Only managers determine how fast it goes
The strongest people should pull the rest
Competition between teams drives progress
questions.why: Lesson 1 compares organizations to the Flintstones' foot-powered bus, which moves only if everyone runs.

questions.q: What does the summary say must accompany high expectations?
a: Clear communication and accountability
Generous bonuses and promotions
Frequent performance reviews
Freedom to choose your own goals
questions.why: Lesson 1 says people need to know exactly what is expected and be held to it.

questions.q: Which group does the summary describe as only running when someone is watching?
a: The riders
The walkers
The joggers
The runners
questions.why: Lesson 2 says riders hide in the crowd and perform only when observed.

questions.q: How does the summary describe the walkers?
a: Steady but slow and wary of change
Fast and full of creative ideas
Consistent with occasional bursts of speed
Eager to lead the whole group
questions.why: Lesson 2 says walkers are steady, rather slow, dislike change and can hold the bus back.

questions.q: What does the summary say about feeling entitled to a reward?
a: You should let it go and become more deserving
It is the fastest route to a promotion
It proves that you value your own work
It is necessary for a meritocracy to function
questions.why: Lesson 3 says nobody owes you recognition, and patience plus real effort is the way forward.
